metadata.description: Azure region for all resources. Defaults to westus3, which has been validated for PostgreSQL Flexible Server B1ms and Azure Container Apps.
Base name for the Azure Support Agent deployment. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.
Immutable container image reference. The default is a published linux/amd64 manifest digest; override only with another reviewed tag or, preferably, registry/repository@sha256:digest reference.

Optional Azure Container Registry login server, for example contoso.azurecr.io. Leave empty for public images. When set, containerRegistryIdentityResourceId must name an existing user-assigned identity with AcrPull on that registry.

Optional existing user-assigned identity resource ID used for private ACR pulls and Key Vault references. Grant AcrPull and/or Key Vault Secrets User before deployment. The app also always receives its own system-assigned runtime identity.
Shared tags merged onto all taggable resources. Supplied values override the built-in Application, Environment, and ManagedBy tags.
Value for the built-in Environment resource tag.
Bootstrap local admin username for first login.
Bootstrap local admin password for first login. User is forced to change it after first sign-in.
PostgreSQL administrator username.
PostgreSQL administrator password. Supply a strong, random value — this is a real credential and there is deliberately no default.
PostgreSQL database name used by the app.
PostgreSQL compute tier. Burstable keeps one-click cost low; use GeneralPurpose or MemoryOptimized before enabling high availability.
PostgreSQL Flexible Server SKU name. It must belong to postgresSkuTier and be offered in the selected region. B1ms is the balanced low-cost default; the production preset uses a General Purpose SKU.
PostgreSQL Premium SSD storage size in GiB. Storage can grow but cannot be reduced after deployment.
Enable PostgreSQL storage autogrow. This prevents disk-full outages but has no configurable cost ceiling, so the one-click default is Disabled and the production preset opts in.
PostgreSQL point-in-time backup retention in days (7-35). Fourteen days balances recoverability and retained-backup cost.
Enable geo-redundant PostgreSQL backups. This is a create-time, region-dependent, higher-cost choice and is disabled by default.
PostgreSQL high-availability mode. SameZone and ZoneRedundant require a supported General Purpose or Memory Optimized SKU and approximately double compute cost.
Optional primary PostgreSQL availability zone. Leave empty for Azure placement; availability varies by region.
Optional PostgreSQL standby availability zone used only with high availability. Leave empty for Azure placement.
Use a custom PostgreSQL maintenance window. Disabled uses the Azure-managed schedule; Enabled uses the day/hour/minute parameters below.
Custom maintenance day, where 0 is Sunday and 6 is Saturday. Used only when postgresCustomMaintenanceWindow is Enabled.
Custom maintenance start hour in the server region local time. Used only when postgresCustomMaintenanceWindow is Enabled.
Custom maintenance start minute. PostgreSQL Flexible Server currently supports the top of the hour.
Container CPU cores. Keep this paired with a supported memory value.
Container memory allocation. Chromium and Azure CLI need headroom, so 2Gi is the default.
Minimum always-running Container App replicas. One controls idle cost; the production preset uses two for replica-level resilience.
Maximum Container App replicas. The balanced default allows one additional replica while limiting database connections and cost.
Concurrent HTTP requests per replica before the Container Apps HTTP scaler adds capacity.
Make the Container Apps environment zone redundant. Disabled preserves regional compatibility and cost; enable only in a supported availability-zone region.
Storage account redundancy for Azure Files. Standard_LRS is the low-cost default; production commonly chooses Standard_ZRS after confirming regional support.
Azure Files share quota in GiB.
Deleted Azure Files shares are recoverable for this many days (1-365).
Optional direct Fernet key for stored application secrets. Prefer secretsEncryptionKeySecretUri; leave both empty to retain the existing generated key on Azure Files.
Optional Key Vault secret URI containing DATABASE_URL. The selected managed identity needs Key Vault Secrets User; leave empty to use the template-created PostgreSQL password secret.
Optional Key Vault secret URI containing the bootstrap admin password. The selected managed identity needs Key Vault Secrets User; leave empty to use adminPassword.
Optional Key Vault secret URI containing SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY. The selected managed identity needs Key Vault Secrets User.
Log Analytics and diagnostic data retention in days (30-730).
Deploy PostgreSQL and Azure Files diagnostic settings to Log Analytics. Container App console/system logs are already connected through the managed environment and are not duplicated.
Deploy the action group and supported platform metric alerts. Disabled by default to avoid notification and alert-rule costs in one-click/dev deployments.

Deploy scheduled-query alerts for event-loop stalls, database-pool exhaustion, probe failures, and platform restart logs. Enable on a later deployment after Container Apps log tables have received data.
Optional email receiver for the generated action group. Leave empty to create an action group without an email receiver and attach receivers later.
PostgreSQL active-connection count that raises an alert. Set below the server max_connections value with room for maintenance and administration.
Container App average response-time alert threshold in milliseconds.
Optional deletion locks on PostgreSQL, storage, and the Container App. CanNotDelete protects data while still allowing updates; None keeps teardown one-click.

Deploy backing storage AND PostgreSQL behind Private Endpoints inside a VNet (Yes) or use the simple public deployment (No). This is a create-time choice and cannot be toggled on an existing deployment.

PUBLIC MODE ONLY — acknowledge that the PostgreSQL server will accept connections from ANY Azure tenant, via the AllowAzureServices 0.0.0.0 rule, because Container Apps egress IPs are not stable. Choose No only when Private networking = Yes, or when you will add your own scoped firewall rules; otherwise the app cannot reach its database. Ignored when Private networking = Yes.
VNet address space (CIDR) used only when Private networking = Yes. Pick a range that does not overlap your existing networks.

Optional. Client IP ranges (CIDR) permitted to reach the application, enforced at the Container Apps ingress before any traffic reaches the container. Leave empty to allow the whole internet. Each entry: { name, description, ipAddressRange }.

How allowedClientIpRanges is applied. Allow = ONLY the listed ranges may connect (everything else is refused). Deny = the listed ranges are refused and everything else is permitted. All entries share this action; they cannot be mixed.

Optional. Comma-separated IPs/CIDRs used to seed the IN-APP allowlist on first boot only, so a new deployment is not open to the internet while waiting for an administrator to configure it. Never overwrites what an admin later saves in the app. Example: 203.0.113.0/24,198.51.100.7

Mode applied to the seeded in-app allowlist. Use monitor to observe what WOULD be blocked without blocking anything, then switch to enforce in the app once the ranges are proven correct. Ignored when allowlistSeed is empty.

Whether the application has a public endpoint. External = reachable from the internet (default). Internal = no public endpoint; reachable only from inside the VNet, which REQUIRES Private networking = Yes and your own connectivity into that VNet (VPN, Bastion, private endpoint or a subnet router).
Infrastructure subnet (CIDR) for the Container Apps Environment. Must be at least a /23 (Container Apps requirement) and inside the VNet address space. Used only when Private networking = Yes.

Private Endpoint subnet (CIDR) for the storage and PostgreSQL private endpoints. Must be inside the VNet address space and not overlap the infrastructure subnet. Used only when Private networking = Yes.

platformMetricAlerts.name: PostgreSQL CPU high
platformMetricAlerts.description: PostgreSQL average CPU exceeded 80 percent for five minutes.

platformMetricAlerts.name: PostgreSQL memory high
platformMetricAlerts.description: PostgreSQL average memory exceeded 85 percent for five minutes.

platformMetricAlerts.name: PostgreSQL connections high
platformMetricAlerts.description: PostgreSQL active connections exceeded the configured threshold.

platformMetricAlerts.name: PostgreSQL storage high
platformMetricAlerts.description: PostgreSQL average storage use exceeded 80 percent for five minutes.

platformMetricAlerts.name: PostgreSQL failed connections
platformMetricAlerts.description: PostgreSQL reported more than five failed connections in five minutes.

platformMetricAlerts.name: Container App HTTP 5xx
platformMetricAlerts.description: The Container App returned one or more server-error responses in five minutes.

platformMetricAlerts.name: Container App replica restarts
platformMetricAlerts.description: A replica cumulative restart counter exceeded three; investigate revision health.

platformMetricAlerts.name: Container App replicas below minimum
platformMetricAlerts.description: Available replicas fell below the configured minimum.

platformMetricAlerts.name: Container App response time high
platformMetricAlerts.description: Average ingress response time exceeded the configured threshold for five minutes.

platformMetricAlerts.name: Azure Files availability low
platformMetricAlerts.description: Azure Files average availability fell below 99 percent for five minutes.

platformMetricAlerts.name: Azure Files capacity high
platformMetricAlerts.description: Azure Files capacity exceeded 80 percent of the configured share quota.

logAlertDefinitions.name: Application readiness and loop health
logAlertDefinitions.description: Application logs reported an event-loop stall, database-pool exhaustion, or readiness failure.
logAlertDefinitions.query: [format('ContainerAppConsoleLogs | where ContainerAppName == ''{0}'' | where Log has_any (''event loop blocked for'', ''QueuePool limit'', ''readiness probe failed'')', variables('containerAppName'))]

logAlertDefinitions.name: Container App platform restart
logAlertDefinitions.description: Container Apps system logs reported a restart event for this application.
logAlertDefinitions.query: [format('ContainerAppSystemLogs | where ContainerAppName == ''{0}'' | where Reason has ''Restart'' or Log has ''restart''', variables('containerAppName'))]
